LESSON: WRITING 2.5.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: PUNCTUATION MARKS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.5: Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to punctuate a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy : Learners develop interacting with technology skills by using digital devices as they play online games and record

dialogues.

● Self-efficacy :Learners develop self-awareness and planning skills as they pay attention to detail while role-playing and recording

dialogues.

Values:
● Unity: is achieved as learners give each other feedback on charts and posters featuring the use of punctuation marks.

Link to other Subjects

The learner relates the concept of proper punctuation to their learning in other learning areas such as Kiswahili and Kenyan Sign Language.

Suggested Learning Resources
